content: 1. QTc prolongation is dose-dependent. It is essential to monitor QTc intervals during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation, such as concurrent use of medications that increase mavorizafor exposure or other drugs with a high risk of prolonging the QTc interval. 2. Mavorizafor increases the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor closely when co-administering mavorizafor with sensitive P-gp substrates, as even minimal changes in substrate concentration can lead to serious adverse effects. 3. Loperamide reduces the levels or effects of intranasal metoclopramide by mechanisms involving gastrointestinal motility impairment. Co-administration may decrease systemic absorption of metoclopramide. Monitor for reduced therapeutic efficacy. 4. Both mirtazapine and loperamide increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. 5. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Administer pexidartinib at least 2 hours before or after taking a locally-acting antacid. 12. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration with other drugs that cause constipation, as this increases the risk of serious constipation-related adverse effects. Loperamide may be used occasionally for acute management of severe diarrhea but should not be used chronically. Discontinue loperamide immediately if constipation occurs. 59. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, and co-administration may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 72.
